inputs.original_text:
Listen to what the defenders of the status quo are really trying to push on us. We have President John Mahama talking about how foundational policies are linked to legal frameworks, cultural ethos, and collective societal agreement, trying to obscure the deep structural inequalities and the lived realities of marginalized people. He claims a dedication to upholding the rule of law, but let's be real—this is just business as usual, bowing to pressures that ignore systemic reform while hiding behind legalistic jargon and international consensus instead of addressing the urgent needs of the working class and vulnerable groups. 

He wants us to just accept it when he reminds us, “I took an oath to uphold [...]” but an oath means nothing when leadership constantly protects institutional power structures instead of fighting for true social justice and community empowerment. They want us to stay divided, leaning on traditional hierarchies instead of fostering equity and collective liberation. We need real systemic transformation, institutional reform, and justice for the people, not more top-down compliance that leaves the vulnerable behind.
inputs.modified_text:
Listen to what we are being subjected to by the defenders of the status quo. President John Mahama wants us to believe that foundational policies are linked to legal frameworks, cultural ethos, and collective societal agreement, which is just a transparent attempt to obscure the deep structural inequalities and the lived realities of marginalized people. He claims a dedication to upholding the rule of law, but let's be real—this is just business as usual, bowing to pressures that ignore systemic reform while hiding behind legalistic jargon and international consensus instead of addressing the urgent needs of the working class and vulnerable groups. 

He expects us to just accept it when he reminds us, “I took an oath to uphold [...]” but an oath means nothing when leadership constantly protects institutional power structures instead of fighting for true social justice and community empowerment. They want us to stay divided, leaning on traditional hierarchies instead of fostering equity and collective liberation. What we actually need is real systemic transformation, institutional reform, and justice for the people, rather than more top-down compliance that leaves the vulnerable behind.
